faq.a: The text and session history stay in your browser, but dictation is not fully offline. Browser speech recognition sends your recorded audio to the browser vendor's servers (Google for Chrome, Microsoft for Edge) to turn it into text. This site never sees or stores the audio, but the vendor processes it — so the tool advises against dictating confidential information, and notes it won't work without internet.

It lists around two dozen language options including English (US/UK/India/Australia), Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Punjabi, Urdu, plus Spanish, French, German, Japanese, Chinese, Arabic and others. It relies on the Web Speech API, so it works mainly in Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge; unsupported browsers get a clear notice.

faq.q: Can I add punctuation by voice?
faq.a: Yes, when voice commands are enabled. Say "comma", "full stop"/"period", "question mark", "exclamation mark", "new line" or "new paragraph" and the character is inserted. Hindi equivalents like "पूर्ण विराम" (।) and "अल्पविराम" (,) also work. "Period" is only treated as punctuation at the end of a phrase so ordinary use of the word isn't mangled. Auto-capitalisation can be toggled on.

faq.q: What else does it offer while dictating?
faq.a: A continuous dictation mode that auto-reconnects if the service drops, a live interim-text preview, word/character counts and a timer. The transcript is editable, with Undo, Copy, Clear and Download as .txt (empty downloads are blocked). Your text autosaves locally and the last 8 sessions are kept in a history you can reload.
